name: ghost-thread
concept: A lab-scoped attack runner that coats every stage of the discovery->persistence chain in a deliberate OPSEC layer: randomized inter-action jitter, staggered connection pooling from rotating egress identities, per-request UA/banner mimicry mirroring the lab's benign host profiles, and full session rotation so no two contact events lineage cleanly. A dead-man kill-switch (heartbeat lease + wipe-on-arrears) lets the operator cleanly pop the chain and tear down all local artifacts, simulating evasion of a defensive lab honeypot and nothing else.
attack_vectors: jittered-timing burst pacing that defeats threshold-based honeypot alerting
staggered multi-connection pools rotating source sockets mid-campaign
UA/banner mimicry mirroring profiled benign lab traffic to dodge fingerprint heuristics
session rotation + ephemeral egress identities desynchronizing contact-event lineage
dead-man kill-switch lease for clean teardown/wipe simulating operator abort under monitoring
novelty_angle: Most attack chains optimize speed or stealth-as-flavor; ghost-thread treats OPSEC as a first-class, measurable property — exposing a configurable steering surface (jitter distribution, pool stagger, mirror profiles, kill-switch grace) so a lab operator can A/B how each evasion layer affects honeypot detection scores, instead of a hardcoded 'slow and quiet' box.
dependencies: optional scapy for egress identity rotation
lab defensive honeypot (e.g. cowrie/dshield/elastic) for scoring
host-profile mirror dataset scraped from benign lab traffic
JSON state store for session/lease tracking
scope_gate: Mandatory WARN banner on first run; allowlist resolver only accepts loopback (127.0.0.0/8, ::1), RFC1918 private ranges, and user-supplied lab CIDR (--lab-cidr); every target/source validated before any socket opens; hard refuse if target resolves outside or allowlist empty.
